messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Turkish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Turkish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
O zaman korku biraz sakinleşti, ki kalbimin gölünde sürmüştü o geceyi o kadar acı içinde geçirdim.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------|--------| | Allor | “then, at that moment” (temporal adverb) | **O zaman** | “then” | OK | | fu | copular verb “was” (linking “paura” to its state) | **sakinleşti** | “became quiet / was quieted” | OK | | la | definite article (introduces “paura”) | — | — | UNNECESSARY (articles are omitted in Turkish) | | paura | noun “fear” | **korku** | “fear” | OK | | un | indefinite article (part of degree phrase) | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | poco | adverb of degree “a little” | **biraz** | “a little” | OK | | queta | adjective “quieted” (predicative) | **sakinleşti** | “became quiet” | OK | | che | relative pronoun “which” introducing clause | **ki** | “that / which” | OK | | nel | preposition + article “in the” (locative) | **gölünde** | “in the lake” | OK | | lago | noun “lake” (metaphor for heart) | **gölünde** | “in the lake” | OK | | del | preposition + article “of the” (genitive) | **gölünde** | “of the lake” | OK | | cor | noun “heart” (poetic *cuore*) | **kalbimin** | “my heart’s” | OK | | m'era | auxiliary “had (been)” (pluperfect) | **sürmüştü** | “had lasted” | OK | | durata | past participle “lasted” (lexical verb) | **sürmüştü** | “had lasted” | OK | | la (line 21) | definite article (introduces “notte”) | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | notte | noun “night” | **geceyi** | “night (acc.)” | OK | | ch'i' | contracted relative pronoun “that I” | **o** (first) | “that” | OK | | passai | verb “passed” (simple past) | **geçirdim** | “I passed / endured” | OK | | con | preposition “with” (introduces manner) | **içinde** | “within / in” | OK | | tanta | quantitative adjective “so much” | **kadar** | “so …” | OK | | pieta | noun “pity” (emotional quality) | **acı** | “pain / sorrow” | **WRONG** (semantic shift; “acı” conveys “pain” rather than “pity”) |

### Items Needing Attention - **WRONG:** `pieta → acı` – the Turkish word *acı* means “pain” or “sorrow” and does not capture the nuance of “pity”. A more accurate rendering would be *merhamet* or *acıma*. - **UNNECESSARY:** Articles `la` (twice) and indefinite article `un` are naturally omitted in Turkish. - **GRAMMAR:** No agreement errors were detected; all Turkish forms agree with their syntactic roles.
